newsitem.title: UK: Nat Grid shares ease after price proposals.
newsitem.headline: Nat Grid shares ease after price proposals.

text.p: Shares in National Grid which runs the electricity transmission network in England and Wales eased in Thursday pre-market trading after the latest price-cutting proposals from industry regulator OFFER.
The proposals, which were at the low end of expectations, included a one-off 20 percent cut in transmission price controls followed by RPI-4 in each of the following three years.
OFFER's initial range for the first-year price cut had been between 20 and 26 percent.
By 0705 GMT the shares were 1p lower at 177-1/2p.

Professor Stephen Littlechild, Director General of Electricity Supply, said the proposals will benefit customers by nearly one billion stg over four years and that they represented a reasonable balance between the interests of customers and shareholders. National Grid is to respond by October 30.
"It's much as expected really and Littlechild hasn't been moved by the protestations of National Grid," said SG Strauss Turnbull analyst Marshall Whiting.
"What National Grid do will be interesting. They have balance the risk of a more severe regulatory regime against one that's going to be fairly tough anyway."

If National Grid accepts the proposals the price control will take effect from April 1. Littlechild said that if the latest plans were not acceptable to National Grid he expected the issue to be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
